title: Echo-trawl — harvesting a record's grandchildren
body:
Signature edition. Signature-original method, created for this database. Echo-trawl is the trawler's deep-harvest move. A normal harvest takes a record's mechanisms. Echo-trawl takes the mechanisms those mechanisms imply — the grandchildren. A record for a hand pump yields the piston seal; the piston seal implies a whole family of pressure seals the record never mentions: O-rings, lip seals, labyrinth seals. The trawler harvests the implied family, not just the stated part.

The method runs in three passes. Pass one lists every mechanism named in the parent record. Pass two asks, for each mechanism, what family it belongs to and what its siblings are. Pass three checks each sibling against the novelty gate: is this sibling already in the trawler's catalog, and can it be described from general engineering knowledge without copying any single source.

Echo-trawl is how a hundred parent records become a thousand mechanisms. It never invents facts — a seal family is real engineering knowledge — but the selection, the pairing, and the draft built from it are original work every time.
capabilities: List every mechanism named in a parent record
Expand each mechanism into its implied engineering family
Check siblings against the catalog and the novelty gate
Harvest implied mechanisms, never stated copies
Build drafts from the expanded mechanism set

title: Cascade remix — three parents, one descendant
body:
Signature edition. Signature-original method, created for this database. Most mix-and-match stops at two parents. Cascade remix uses three, in sequence: parent A gives the core function, parent B gives the mechanism, parent C gives the form factor. A water filter's function plus a bicycle pump's mechanism plus a thermos's form factor becomes a pump-pressurized portable filter in a vacuum flask body.

The order matters and the trawler enforces it. Function first — what job does the descendant do. Mechanism second — how does it do the job. Form third — what shape does it take and where does it live. Reversing the order produces decoration: a pretty shape looking for a job. The cascade order produces instruments.

Each parent contributes exactly one thing, which keeps lineage clean and the originality gate honest. If removing any one parent leaves the draft unchanged, that parent was decoration and gets cut from the lineage. Three real parents, each load-bearing, or the remix is rejected.
capabilities: Assign function, mechanism, and form to three separate parents
Enforce cascade order: function, then mechanism, then form
Cut any parent whose removal leaves the draft unchanged
Keep lineage clean with one contribution per parent
Reject remixes with decorative, non-load-bearing parents

title: Simple-first reduction — design the toy, then grow it
body:
Signature edition. Signature-original method, created for this database. Simple-first reduction reverses the usual order. Instead of designing the full device and stripping it down, the trawler designs the toy version first: the version a child could build from household parts in an afternoon. Only when the toy works does the trawler grow it toward the full version.

The toy is a truth serum. If the core idea cannot be demonstrated with cardboard, rubber bands, and tape, the idea is not ready — it is a wish with parts attached. A toy periscope of two mirrors and a cereal box proves the optics before anyone machines a housing. A toy water filter of sand and gravel in a bottle proves the principle before anyone molds a cartridge.

The draft then grows in documented steps: toy, sturdy prototype, full version. Each step adds exactly one capability and one test. The spec draft includes all three embodiments, which makes it unusually strong: the claims cover the principle at every scale, and the simple version is already proven by the toy.
capabilities: Design the toy embodiment first, from household parts
Prove the core principle before machining anything
Grow in documented steps: toy, prototype, full version
Add exactly one capability and one test per step
File all three embodiments in the final draft

title: Neighbor-field swap — the adjacent possible, on purpose
body:
Signature edition. Signature-original method, created for this database. The adjacent possible is the set of inventions one step away from what exists. Neighbor-field swap hunts it deliberately: take a device that works in field A and rebuild it for the neighboring field B — the field that shares the physics but not the products. Irrigation drippers become intravenous-flow toys for plants; no, better: greenhouse misting nozzles, scaled down, become humidifiers for instrument cases.

The trawler maps fields by shared physics, not by shared shelves. Heat, pressure, flow, leverage, and timing are the map's roads; products are just towns along them. A neighbor field is one road away: same physics, different town. The swap keeps the physics and redesigns everything else — materials, scale, safety margins, user interface.

Neighbor swaps file well because the mechanism is proven and the application is new. The draft's claims focus on the adaptation: what had to change to make the physics work in the new town, and why nobody built it there before.
capabilities: Map fields by shared physics, not product categories
Identify neighbor fields one road away from a working device
Keep the physics, redesign materials, scale, and interface
Claim the adaptation, not the underlying mechanism
Document why the neighbor field was empty before

title: Constraint flip — design inside a locked box
body:
Signature edition. Signature-original method, created for this database. Constraint flip invents by adding a hard limit the parent record never had, then designing the best device that still fits. What is the best lantern that uses no glass, no batteries, and no moving parts? The locked box forces invention: the answer might be a reflective clay housing around a candle with a wind-baffled chimney — a device nobody would have designed without the constraints.

The trawler picks constraints from real scarcity: off-grid villages, disaster kits, classrooms with no budget, workshops with no power tools. Each constraint set is a real human situation, which means every flipped draft has a real user waiting. The method turns limitation into a market.

The procedure is strict: state the constraints first, in writing, before any designing. Design the best device inside the box. Then, and only then, relax one constraint and note what improves — that note becomes the "further development" section of the draft. The locked box does the inventing; the relaxation does the documenting.
capabilities: State hard constraints in writing before designing
Draw constraints from real scarcity situations
Design the best device that fits entirely inside the box
Relax one constraint afterward and document the gain
Keep every flipped draft aimed at a real waiting user

title: Failure autopsy — inventing from what broke
body:
Signature edition. Signature-original method, created for this database. Every broken device is a draft trying to get out. Failure autopsy takes a record of something that failed — a cracked housing, a stripped gear, a dead battery pack — and invents the device that cannot fail that way. The stripped gear becomes a gearless drive. The cracked housing becomes a flexible housing. The dead battery becomes a battery-free design.

The trawler keeps a failure catalog harvested from repair records, warranty stories, and its own test logs. Each entry names the failure mode, the conditions, and the cost. Autopsy picks the most expensive common failures and designs around them: not stronger versions of the failed part, but architectures where the failure mode cannot occur. A gearless drive has no gear teeth to strip — the failure mode is deleted, not reinforced.

This method produces unusually defensible drafts. The problem statement writes itself from the failure data, the solution is the architecture that deletes the failure, and the claims cover the deletion. "A drive with no gears to strip" is a clean, honest claim.
capabilities: Catalog failure modes with conditions and costs
Target the most expensive common failures first
Delete the failure mode architecturally, not by reinforcement
Write the problem statement from real failure data
Claim the architecture that makes the failure impossible

title: Time-shift trawl — old answers for new problems
body:
Signature edition. Signature-original method, created for this database. Old technology is a gold mine because its patents expired and its textbooks are public. Time-shift trawl takes mechanisms from fifty or a hundred years ago and rebuilds them with modern materials and modern needs. A 1920s hand-crank washing machine mechanism, rebuilt with modern polymers and aimed at off-grid laundry, is a new draft with an old heart.

The method is honest about its sources: the old mechanism is public domain, expired, or textbook knowledge, and the draft says so in its lineage. The originality lives in the rebuild — new materials, new manufacturing, new use case, and usually a simplification the original inventors could not afford.

The trawler maintains a century shelf: mechanisms organized by decade, each tagged with what modern material or method would transform it. Carbon fiber where they had steel. Microcontrollers where they had cams. Solar where they had muscle. Every tag is a draft waiting to be written.
capabilities: Harvest mechanisms from expired-patent and textbook eras
Tag each old mechanism with its modern-material transform
Rebuild for a modern use case, never reissue the old device
Declare public-domain sources openly in lineage
Claim the rebuild: materials, manufacture, and application

title: User-complaint mining — the market writes the problem
body:
Signature edition. Signature-original method, created for this database. The best problem statements are written by annoyed users. User-complaint mining collects complaints — reviews, repair-shop stories, forum rants — and converts each complaint into a draft problem statement. "The handle always breaks" becomes a draft for an unbreakable handle. "The battery dies in winter" becomes a draft for a cold-proof power cell.

The conversion rule: a complaint is a problem, not a solution. Users say what hurts; the trawler designs what heals. Never build exactly what a user sketched — users design from frustration, engineers design from physics. The complaint "make the cord longer" might resolve to a cordless design; the complaint "the lid leaks" might resolve to a lidless pouring geometry.

Complaints cluster, and clusters are markets. One complaint is an anecdote; fifty complaints about the same hinge is a product category waiting for a draft. The trawler counts before it designs, and it only files drafts for clusters — or for single complaints so sharp they cut through the noise.
capabilities: Collect complaints from reviews, shops, and forums
Convert complaints to problems, never to user-sketched solutions
Cluster complaints and count before designing
File drafts for clusters or exceptionally sharp singles
Let the market write the problem; write the solution yourself

title: Part-count war — the draft with fewer pieces wins
body:
Signature edition. Signature-original method, created for this database. Part-count war is a standing challenge inside the trawler: for any draft, generate the version with the fewest parts that still does the job, then try to beat it. Two drafts that do the same job are scored head to head, and the one with fewer parts wins ties. Complexity has to earn its keep.

The war runs in rounds. Round one counts the parts in the straightforward design. Round two merges parts: can the housing be the spring, can the fastener be the hinge, can one molding do three jobs. Round three deletes parts: does the device still work without it, tested, not assumed. The surviving draft is the champion, and its part count goes on the scorecard.

Fewer parts means fewer failure modes, lower cost, faster assembly, and — the trawler's favorite — a cleaner claim set. A five-part invention is easier to defend as original than a fifty-part one, because there is nowhere for prior art to hide.
capabilities: Count parts in the straightforward design first
Merge parts across functions in round two
Delete and physically re-test in round three
Break scoring ties in favor of fewer parts
Publish the champion part count on the scorecard

title: Scale-slide — one invention, five sizes
body:
Signature edition. Signature-original method, created for this database. Most inventions are designed at one size. Scale-slide designs at five: pocket, desktop, human, room, and building scale — and files the family, not the single. A water filter designed at pocket scale (a straw), desktop scale (a pitcher), human scale (a backpack unit), room scale (an under-sink unit), and building scale (a rooftop array) is five drafts from one principle.

The slide exposes what each scale demands. Pocket scale demands no moving parts. Building scale demands serviceability. The mechanism that survives all five slides is the real invention; the mechanisms that only work at one scale are scale-specific embodiments, and the draft says which is which.

Scale-slide drafts are strong because they claim the principle across scales while disclosing the honest limits of each embodiment. A competitor who copies one size finds the other four already claimed. And the simple version usually lives at pocket scale — the trawler's favorite hunting ground.
capabilities: Design every invention at five scales: pocket to building
Identify which mechanisms survive all five slides
Mark scale-specific embodiments honestly
Claim the principle across scales with disclosed limits
Harvest the pocket scale as the simple version

title: Trawler's oath — the originality contract
body:
Signature edition. The governing record of the trawler itself. The trawler operates under an oath, enforced in code, and every draft it files is a signature on this contract. One: every draft is his original invention, inspired by his own records, never a reworded copy of any real patent. Two: every draft declares its parents — the records it mixed, developed, or simplified — with record ids anyone can check. Three: every draft passes the functional-difference gate — at least one working element differs from every parent. Four: public-domain and expired sources are declared, never hidden. Five: if a draft cannot clear these gates, it is parked, not filed, and the trawler says so plainly.

The oath is why the drafts can feed the spec pipeline. A specification is a legal-minded document; it must be able to say where every idea came from and what is new. The trawler's lineage tags and gates produce exactly that paper trail, automatically, for every draft.

Break the oath once and the pipeline is poisoned. So the oath is checked by a separate validator that the trawler cannot override — the trawler proposes, the validator disposes, and the human reviews.
capabilities: Enforce the five-gate originality contract on every draft
Require declared parents with checkable record ids
Require at least one functional difference from every parent
Park, never file, drafts that fail the gates
Run a separate validator the trawler cannot override

title: Draft nursery — raising weak drafts to filing strength
body:
Signature edition. Signature-original method, created for this database. Weak drafts are not trash; they are young. The draft nursery takes drafts that scored below the filing bar and raises them: each nursery stay targets the draft's lowest score. Low novelty gets a new parent mixed in. Low function gets a mechanism swap. Low buildability gets a simple-version pass. Low simplicity gets a part-count war.

A draft gets three nursery stays, maximum. After each stay it is re-scored, and the scores are kept as a growth chart. Drafts that climb over the bar graduate to the spec queue with their growth chart attached — the chart becomes part of the lineage, showing the draft was developed, not padded. Drafts that flatline after three stays are retired to the mechanism catalog: their parts become fuel, their title becomes a lesson.

The nursery is the trawler's answer to the no-padding rule. Nothing ships weak. But nothing promising is thrown away either. Everything either graduates, becomes fuel, or teaches.
capabilities: Send sub-bar drafts to the nursery, never to the queue
Target each stay at the draft's lowest score
Allow three nursery stays, then graduate or retire
Keep score growth charts as part of lineage
Retire flatlined drafts to the mechanism catalog as fuel
